scope: local ARM64 Mac/Docker80k-user four-shard fixed-load comparison; not an official score or capacity search

protocol.paired_random_stream: same native run-id and VU ids within each pair; fresh DBs prevent name collisions
protocol.warmup: none; this is a fixed-load diagnostic, not the official warmup/search/hold protocol
protocol.invalid_policy: native lg_limited or failed infrastructure is INVALID; retain, never replace
protocol.interpretation: at fixed unsaturated load, compare latency/CPU; similar req/s cannot establish capacity

proposal_label: Same frozen Goose binary: WORKERS=2 / ARTICLE_BATCH=1 vs unchanged Rust #7
preconditions: The current three-pair study finishes and its results are retained before execution.
In a quiet interval, the unchanged conformance suite passes 197/197 with WORKERS=2 and ARTICLE_BATCH=1.
Frozen source/binary/tool hashes match the reference study. No compiler/source/default change is included.
Actual running challenge UID and nofile >= 200000 are verified by the existing v3 launcher.

preregistered_acceptance.claims_scope: Local fixed 80k-user diagnostic only; no capacity, official ranking, or all-competitor superiority claim.
preregistered_acceptance.hypothesis: Lower fan-out lets compatible reads coalesce while cutting PostgreSQL backend/scheduling overhead; live article batching may reduce repeated metadata work at this load. Both changes are tested together, so the study cannot attribute individual effects.
preregistered_acceptance.clean_pair_definition: All 6 prescheduled attempts classify PASS, with zero HTTP/socket/timeout errors, valid frozen target/load/host witnesses, no target OOM and zero target swap, all 80k VUs active, and no native generator-limited verdict. Existing v3 host-memory criteria are unchanged. Invalid/failing attempts are retained and block acceptance; never replace them selectively.

metric.name: whole_target_cpu_seconds_per_successful_request
metric.scope: Combined app + PostgreSQL target cgroup, using the existing fully bracketed v3 target monitor. The CPU average uses the sampled interval inside the 60-second native request window. App-only CPU cannot substitute.
metric.limitation: CPU/request is a fixed-load sampled estimate; it does not measure maximum user capacity.

preregistered_acceptance.promotion_policy: No speed claim or default promotion unless every pair individually passes all criteria. Do not pool away a worse pair,change thresholds after seeing results,or treat equal closed-model req/s as a capacity win. A passing combined experiment still requires separate evidence before attributing gains to either setting.
